question: What percentage of tests will be positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 1 (New England) for the week ending September 26, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 1 (New England) for the week ending 2026-09-26 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
I could not get a version of the dataset frozen at 2026-09-07. The CDC dataset is overwritten every week. So I took the summer 2026 rows below from the current version and left out all rows dated after the cutoff. Values for recent weeks may have been revised a little since they were first posted.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the CDC NREVSS dataset rgnm-fkqb, filtered to level "Region 1" and pathogen "RSV", using the field percent_pos for week ending 2026-09-26, as posted 2026-10-30. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json?level=Region%201&pathogen=RSV&$order=mmwrweek_end%20DESC&$limit=200)
- 2026-08-29: the latest week likely public by 2026-09-07 shows 0.40% positive (1,748 tests). [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json?level=Region%201&pathogen=RSV&$order=mmwrweek_end%20DESC&$limit=200)
- 2026-09-05: the dataset now shows 0.16%, with the test count suppressed (shown as "*"). This week was probably not public yet on 2026-09-07. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json?level=Region%201&pathogen=RSV&$order=mmwrweek_end%20DESC&$limit=200)
- Weeks with very few positive tests have their counts suppressed but still show a percent.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. RSV in New England is at its usual low point between seasons. Each week has about 1,500 to 1,800 tests, so a handful of positives can move the rate by several tenths of a point.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-09-03: a summary of CDC briefings says RSV activity is low in most of the US. [IZ Summit Partners](https://www.izsummitpartners.org/wp-content/uploads/2026_09_03_swu_summary.pdf)
- 2026-09-03: the BC CDC monthly report for 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-29 describes US RSV as very low in most areas. [BCCDC](https://www.bccdc.ca/Health-Info-Site/Documents/Respiratory_data/respiratory_surveillance_2026-09-03.pdf)
- 2026-05-08: the 2025-26 RSV season was unusually late. It peaked in February, and in Region 1 it was still at 1-2% in May. [Drug Topics](https://www.drugtopics.com/view/unusual-rsv-rates-increased-in-early-2026-decreasing-in-may)
- CDC's 2026-27 season outlook expects the combined peak hospitalization rate for COVID-19, flu and RSV to be within 20% of last season's peak (low to moderate confidence). It also notes that the national RSV peak usually comes in late December or early January. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-qualitative-assessments/php/data-research/season-outlook26-27.html)

## 4. Base rates
Summer 2026 in Region 1 is running higher than summer 2024 or 2025:
- July to August 2026: weekly values ran from 0.23% to 0.92%. Recent weeks: 0.31 (08-01), 0.92 (08-08), 0.63 (08-15), 0.23 (08-22), 0.40 (08-29).
- July to August 2025: mostly 0.05% to 0.46%.
- July to August 2024: 0.11% to 0.44%.

Change from early September to the last week of September in past years:

| Year | Late Aug / early Sep | Week nearest Sep 26 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 0.46 (08-30), 0.23 (09-06) | 0.39 (09-27); 0.43 (09-20) | about flat to slightly up |
| 2024 | 0.25 (08-31), 0.21 (09-07) | 0.48 (09-28); 0.27 (09-21); 0.03 (09-14) | up about 0.2 to 0.3 |
| 2023 | 0.99 (09-02), 1.48 (09-09) | 2.59 (09-30); 1.72 (09-23) | up about 1 to 1.5 (early season) |
| 2022 | not in the rows I retrieved (they start 2022-12-31) | - | - |

- Typical pattern: late September is about level with, or 0.1 to 0.3 points above, late August. The exception is an early season like 2023, which pushed late September to around 2 to 2.6%. That is at or above the question's 2.5% ceiling.
- Noise: from one week to the next, the rate moves by about ±0.2 to 0.5 points at these levels. For example, it went 0.31 to 0.92 to 0.63 to 0.23 in August 2026.
- 2025 for comparison: 0.31 on 09-13, 0.43 on 09-20, 0.39 on 09-27, then 0.44 to 0.65 in October. The 2025-26 season started late.
- 2026 so far is running above 2024 and 2025 for the same weeks but well below 2023.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets on this series.
- The only related expert view I found is CDC's qualitative outlook for the 2026-27 season (section 3). I found no quantitative regional forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- CDC posts NREVSS updates weekly. Week ending 09-12 should appear around 09-18, week ending 09-19 around 09-25, and week ending 09-26 around 10-02. Later postings, through the 10-30 version that decides the question, may revise the number slightly.
- Schools reopening in late August and September usually brings RSV back gradually, so watch whether early September rises above about 0.5%.
- The weather has little direct effect over a three-week window. I did not look up a seasonal outlook.
- New England states (Massachusetts, Connecticut and others) publish their own weekly respiratory dashboards, which could give early signals.
